- tests/test_internal_review_push_pr_grace.py: Line or code reference: test_invalid_grace_falls_back_to_default_with_warning at lines 197-204 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The invalid-value test asserts that values above the 3600 ceiling fall back to the default, but there is no test for the exact boundary value `CLAUDE_BRANCH_PUSH_PR_GRACE_SECONDS=3600`, which is the only legal value at the upper end of the allowed range.
  WHY: The arithmetic check `[ "$((10#${pr_grace_secs}))" -gt "${pr_grace_max_secs}" ]` uses `>` not `-ge`, so 3600 must be accepted, but that contract is not pinned. Without a boundary test, a regression that turns the comparison into `-ge` (or an off-by-one in `pr_grace_max_secs`) would only surface when an operator sets the variable to 3600.
- .github/workflows/internal-review.yml: Line or code reference: step `resolve`, line ~134 (`pr_lookup_err_file="$(mktemp)"`) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `mktemp` temp file used to capture `gh api`'s stderr is created but never explicitly cleaned up via an EXIT trap.
  WHY: On a public-repo `ubuntu-latest` runner the file is reclaimed when the runner is destroyed, so the leak is bounded, but the step runs on every push to a `claude/**` branch and leaves a `/tmp/tmp.*` file behind each time the lookup fails.
